A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaTT research, with matching authors, core equations and algorithms. The main text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original GLUE fine-tuning, multi-task, initialization and rank-adaptation experiments in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical studies and adds Llama-2 commonsense evaluations and further tensor-adapter and multi-task baseline results.

M1.justification: The shared 4D/5D TT adapters, optional task core, forward update and bidirectional truncated-SVD sweep are retained. Algorithm 1 moves into Section 2.4 without changing its steps. Different initialization settings for the new Llama experiments and revised implementation pseudocode do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds Commonsense170k training and evaluation on ARC-c, ARC-e, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, SIQA and WinoGrande (Table 1), substantially extending v1's GLUE coverage. Three-task and four-task GLUE settings, including QNLI, already existed in v1 and are retained.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds evaluated LoRETTA_adp and LoRTA baselines to v1's LoRA/VeRA/LoTR comparison. Tables 3 and 5 add dedicated MTL-LoRA and MoE-LoRA comparisons. The new Llama comparison also includes a zero-shot reference. These are substantive additions to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: The new Llama experiments introduce 7B/13B models, two-epoch training and best-result selection, and lm-evaluation-harness evaluation. Added baseline experiments introduce their own rank grids, configurations and training budgets (Appendix D.5). The retained MetaTT GLUE protocol, frozen classifier heads and multi-task sampling caps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Table 5 adds a controlled MetaTT-4D versus MetaTT-(4+1)D comparison for four-task learning; v1's four-task analysis showed task-core gradients and training curves without that control. Initialization, projection-selection, gradient and MRPC/RTE rank-adaptation analyses are retained. Consolidating the DMRG plots does not add an experiment.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports the new Llama results as single-shot, without uncertainty estimates, and states that selected LoRA reruns use MetaTT's seeds. Existing GLUE two/three-trial reporting, DMRG ten/four-trial counts and standard-error conventions are retained. No general increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds Llama scores, tensor/MTL baseline results and aggregate four-task comparisons. Between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2, RoBERTa-large LoRA RTE changes from 53(0) to 87.0(8) following reruns of failed imported results; MetaTT-4D rank-32 CoLA changes from 63.3(7) to 64.0(1). The LoTR rank-32 row is omitted. DMRG rank-4 means in v2 Table 4 reproduce v1's figure legends.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2.3 adds the formal condition r > (D/H)(1 - 1/H) under which MetaTT-4D uses fewer parameters than MetaTT-5D, and gives the multi-task parameter count 2Dr + (L + M + T)r^2. Existing factorizations are retained; no substantial theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 claims the greatest parameter reduction, advantages over other tensor methods, and increasing relative performance against LoRA with model size. V2 narrows the central single-task claim to competitive tradeoffs and explicitly acknowledges similarity to other tensor adapters. It strengthens multi-task positioning through comparisons with dedicated methods and a claim that joint tensor-adapter MTL was previously unexplored.

C2.justification: The new four-task discussion qualifies task-core benefits: the extra core improves the larger model's average but slightly worsens the smaller model's average. V2 also acknowledges limited single-task differentiation and hypothesizes analogous MTL extensions for other tensor architectures. Existing initialization-sensitivity limitations move to Appendix F without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Appendix D substantially expands Llama and baseline initialization, hyperparameter grids, learning rates, budgets and RoBERTa adaptation details. Section 5 adds a reproducibility statement. Appendix E revises pseudocode, including parameter registration and a condensed forward pass, although the latter introduces an undefined self.M_2 reference. This does not establish a new MetaTT code release.

R1.justification: V2 more explicitly positions MetaTT as extending LoTR/FacT's 3D tensors and LoRTA's head factorization, emphasizing multi-task use and TT-specific optimization. It adds discussion of VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, MultiLoRA, MoE-LoRA and tensor expressivity, alongside the stronger joint-MTL novelty claim. This substantially revises research positioning beyond relocating related work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, replacing the contribution list with question-led motivation. The DMRG algorithm moves from experiments into methods; related work, implementation settings and limitations are reorganized into appendices. A reproducibility section is added. These changes substantially reshape the narrative independently of the new experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an additional task-adapter panel. V1 Figures 2 and 6 become v2's four-panel Figure 2, with existing rank-4 summaries moved into Table 4. New benchmark and settings tables, expanded baseline tables, boxed table rules, changed typography and wider text areas substantially revise the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the credibility of the central comparisons by rerunning failed imported LoRA results, adding relevant tensor and multi-task baselines, and moderating v1's superiority claims. Llama evaluations and expanded experimental documentation broaden the supporting evidence. These gains outweigh limited new reproducibility problems, although single-shot Llama results and inconsistent MoE-LoRA ranks between Tables 3/5 and Appendix D.5.6 still limit confidence.
